prompt: Why model a mutable object as a hash instead of one string holding serialized JSON?
explanation: A hash lets the application update or read single fields (HSET/HGET) without shipping the whole object, while a JSON string forces a read-modify-write of the entire value for every field change. Hashes do not support per-field TTLs, are not always smaller than JSON, and strings can hold any serialized bytes — those claims are all false.

options.text: Individual fields can be read and updated without read-modify-write of the whole value
Hash fields can each carry their own TTL
Hashes are always smaller in memory than an equivalent JSON string
Strings cannot hold serialized JSON, so a hash is the only option
